newsitem.title: CANADA: Pratt & Whitney gets C$147 mln from Canada.
newsitem.headline: Pratt & Whitney gets C$147 mln from Canada.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Friday it would give United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney Canada C$147 million in two investments aimed at keeping and creating more than 1,000 jobs in Montreal, Halifax and across Canada.
"Aerospace is a crucial sector for Canada's economy, with exports growing at a rate of 10 percent a year," Industry Minister John Manley said in a statement.
The investments, which were made under Ottawa's Technology Partnerships Canada program, were announced in Longueuil, Quebec and Halifax.

A C$100 million repayable investment will allow Pratt & Whitney to complete work on its 6,500 SHP PW150 turboprop engine, which is used on large high-speed regional aircraft like the Dash 8-400 made by Bombardier Inc's majority-owned de Havilland unit.

The investment will also create 260 jobs in research and development in the Montreal area over the next four years, Industry Canada said in a statement. Production of the engines will also create another 490 jobs in Montreal and 200 jobs in Halifax, as well as another 260 jobs for suppliers over the next 15 years, the statement said.
A second C$47 million investment is aimed at helping Pratt & Whitney maintain high levels of research and development and keep 135 jobs over the next three years.
Technology Partnerships Canada provides government investments in specific projects. The often interest-free investments are to be repaid in the form of royalties as products go to the market.
Bombardier or its units have received a total of C$180 million in investments or loans from Ottawa since October. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
